title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — Premium Revision Paper #1

pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the abbreviation 'n.' mean in a dictionary entry? (1 mark)
   A. number
   B. name
   C. noun
   D. never

2. Which article do we use before 'honest man'? (1 mark)
   A. some
   B. an
   C. the
   D. a

3. What should you do first when you get a form? (1 mark)
   A. Fold it
   B. Start writing at once
   C. Read the instructions
   D. Sign it

4. How would you write 9 January 2016 as day, month and year? (1 mark)
   A. 01/09/2016
   B. 2016/01/09 only
   C. 09/01/2016
   D. 9-2016

5. In a readers' theatre, learners (1 mark)
   A. build a stage from wood
   B. sing without words
   C. read a story aloud with different parts
   D. draw pictures only

6. What is the plural of 'tooth'? (1 mark)
   A. teeths
   B. toothes
   C. teeth
   D. tooths

7. Which is a good way to make a story interesting? (1 mark)
   A. Add small details and one simile
   B. Write very short words
   C. Copy a friend
   D. Leave out the ending

8. Which is a linking word that shows something happened at the end? (1 mark)
   A. next
   B. then
   C. finally
   D. first

9. A factual question has an answer that (1 mark)
   A. is stated in the text
   B. you invent
   C. is a joke
   D. is not in the text

10. Which is the best first step before answering a question on a passage? (1 mark)
   A. Read the question and find key words
   B. Close the book
   C. Copy the passage
   D. Write the answer immediately

11. Why should there be a gap between words? (1 mark)
   A. So that the words are easy to read
   B. To make the page dirty
   C. To use more paper
   D. To hide mistakes

12. Which visual would help you find a place you have never been to? (1 mark)
   A. A map
   B. A poem
   C. A joke
   D. A recipe

13. Which is a part of an SMS? (1 mark)
   A. The salutation address
   B. The stamp
   C. The envelope
   D. The message

14. Which sentence would be best in the body of a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. Sincerely, the Manager
   B. To whom it may concern
   C. Yours faithfully
   D. I hope you are well.

15. What is a good habit for a listener? (1 mark)
   A. Play with things
   B. Talk while others speak
   C. Look away
   D. Look at the speaker and do not interrupt

16. A narrative is (1 mark)
   A. a list of names
   B. a map
   C. a story that tells what happened
   D. a form

17. At the end of a statement, the voice usually (1 mark)
   A. shouts
   B. falls
   C. rises
   D. hides

18. Which is a rule for staying safe on the internet? (1 mark)
   A. Open messages from strangers
   B. Tell everyone your password
   C. Share your address
   D. Use it with a parent or teacher

19. Quantifiers: Choose the correct sentence. (1 mark)
   A. How many waters do you drink?
   B. How many water do you drink?
   C. How much water do you drink?
   D. How much waters do you drink?

20. Choose the correct -ing form of 'run'. (1 mark)
   A. runnning
   B. runeing
   C. running
   D. runing

21. Which month is written correctly? (1 mark)
   A. Septembar
   B. Septmber
   C. Septembre
   D. September

22. Which word helps to show the order of events? (1 mark)
   A. green
   B. heavy
   C. farm
   D. suddenly

23. What should you do before writing a narrative? (1 mark)
   A. Make a short plan
   B. Write the ending only
   C. Skip the beginning
   D. Copy someone else's story

24. In which word does 'gh' say /f/? (1 mark)
   A. daughter
   B. high
   C. night
   D. laugh

25. Which word begins with a silent h? (1 mark)
   A. hand
   B. house
   C. help
   D. honest

26. Where does the comma go? (1 mark)
   A. Yes I will help,
   B. Yes, I will help.
   C. Yes I, will help.
   D. Yes I will, help.

27. Which sentence puts the comma after the opening phrase? (1 mark)
   A. In the morning, we do exercises.
   B. In the morning we, do exercises.
   C. In the morning we do, exercises.
   D. In, the morning we do exercises.

28. Which sentence has a comma before 'but' joining two full sentences? (1 mark)
   A. I was tired, but I finished sweeping.
   B. I was tired but, I finished sweeping.
   C. I was tired but I finished sweeping,
   D. I was, tired but I finished sweeping.

29. What is at the centre of a mind map? (1 mark)
   A. The main topic
   B. The author's name
   C. The date
   D. The last idea

30. In which order do we read comic panels? (1 mark)
   A. Left to right and top to bottom
   B. Any order
   C. Right to left
   D. Bottom to top

31. Which word completes 'The coach is asking, "____ scored the goal?"'? (1 mark)
   A. Whose
   B. Who
   C. When
   D. Where

32. Which of these is a homophone pair? (1 mark)
   A. their and there
   B. run and walk
   C. hot and cold
   D. big and large

33. Which is a factual question about the passage? (1 mark)
   A. Why do you think the head teacher smiled?
   B. What job did Class Six do?
   C. What kind of person is Kamau?
   D. Was the clean-up a success?

34. What is the past participle of 'go'? (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. goed
   C. went
   D. gone

35. Which tense do we usually use for earlier events in a diary? (1 mark)
   A. Question form
   B. Past tense
   C. Command
   D. Future tense

36. In which word is the letter b silent? (1 mark)
   A. bag
   B. baby
   C. bus
   D. debt

37. What does 'profit' mean? (1 mark)
   A. A gift
   B. Money lost in a sale
   C. Money gained when you sell for more than you paid
   D. A tax

38. What should you do if a website you find online worries you? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore the adult
   B. Close it and tell a trusted adult
   C. Give your address
   D. Share it with everyone

39. Which word ends with a double consonant? (1 mark)
   A. cla
   B. clasp
   C. clas
   D. class

40. Which is the correct spelling of the word that tells where you live? (1 mark)
   A. adres
   B. adress
   C. addres
   D. address

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. State two things you can find in a dictionary entry. (2 marks)

42. Explain the difference between a fact and an opinion. Give one example of each. (3 marks)

43. Punctuate: 'mama may i go to the shop' (2 marks)

44. State three materials you can read for pleasure. (3 marks)

45. Join with a suitable conjunction: 'I was tired. I finished sweeping.' (2 marks)

46. What is a nonverbal cue? Give two examples. (3 marks)

47. Correct this sentence and explain: 'I don't have no seeds.' (3 marks)

48. From the passage about Mama Neema, what can you tell about her character? Give a reason. (3 marks)

49. Give directions from your classroom to the school gate using at least three prepositions. (3 marks)

50. List two facts from the story about how HIV cannot spread. (2 marks)

51. Change these adjectives into adverbs: gentle, angry, quick. (3 marks)

52. Rewrite in the plural: 'The child put a loaf and a tomato in the box.' (3 marks)

53. Explain the difference between 'my' and 'mine'. Use each in a sentence. (3 marks)

54. Rewrite in the past tense: 'Today we sweep the compound and plant a tree.' (2 marks)

55. Describe the steps to fill in a form correctly. (4 marks)

56. Write the -ing form of each verb: make, run, play, lie. (4 marks)

57. Explain how you can feel the difference between /t/ and /d/ using your throat. (2 marks)

58. State two habits of a good listener. (2 marks)

59. Write an SMS inviting a friend to your birthday party on Saturday at 3 o'clock. (3 marks)

60. Explain the difference in position of 'enough' with a noun and with an adjective. Give an example of each. (4 marks)

61. Rewrite using the past perfect: 'The bus left. Then I arrived.' (2 marks)

62. Name two visuals you can find in a newspaper. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — noun
   The letter n. shows that the word is a noun.

2. B — an
   The h in honest is silent, so an is used.

3. C — Read the instructions
   Instructions tell you how to fill in the form.

4. C — 09/01/2016
   Day first, then month, then year.

5. C — read a story aloud with different parts
   Each reader takes a part and reads the lines.

6. C — teeth
   Tooth is irregular.

7. A — Add small details and one simile
   Details and similes help the reader picture the story.

8. C — finally
   Finally introduces the last event.

9. A — is stated in the text
   Factual answers can be found in the words of the passage.

10. A — Read the question and find key words
   Key words tell you what to look for in the text.

11. A — So that the words are easy to read
   Gaps make the writing legible.

12. A — A map
   A map shows where places are.

13. D — The message
   An SMS has a receiver, a message and a sender.

14. D — I hope you are well.
   It is a warm, friendly opening line.

15. D — Look at the speaker and do not interrupt
   Good listeners give attention.

16. C — a story that tells what happened
   It tells events in order.

17. B — falls
   Statements usually end with a fall.

18. D — Use it with a parent or teacher
   A trusted adult keeps you safe.

19. C — How much water do you drink?
   Water is uncountable.

20. C — running
   Short verbs ending in one vowel and one consonant double the last letter.

21. D — September
   September is spelt with a capital S and the ending -ber.

22. D — suddenly
   'Suddenly' is a time word.

23. A — Make a short plan
   A plan helps organise beginning, middle and end.

24. D — laugh
   'Gh' says /f/ in laugh, cough, enough and rough.

25. D — honest
   'Honest' is said 'onest'.

26. B — Yes, I will help.
   A comma follows 'Yes'.

27. A — In the morning, we do exercises.
   A comma follows the opening phrase.

28. A — I was tired, but I finished sweeping.
   A comma comes before but when joining two full sentences.

29. A — The main topic
   The main topic is in the middle.

30. A — Left to right and top to bottom
   We read a comic like a book.

31. B — Who
   'Who' asks about a person.

32. A — their and there
   They sound the same but are spelt differently.

33. B — What job did Class Six do?
   The answer is stated in the text.

34. D — gone
   Go, went, gone.

35. B — Past tense
   Events that already happened use the past tense.

36. D — debt
   'Debt' is said 'det'.

37. C — Money gained when you sell for more than you paid
   Profit is the gain from selling.

38. B — Close it and tell a trusted adult
   Staying safe means asking for help.

39. D — class
   Class ends in ss.

40. D — address
   Address has a double d and a double s.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two: spelling, meaning, part of speech, example sentence, pronunciation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: A fact can be checked, for example 'Germs are tiny'. An opinion says what someone thinks, for example 'Cold water is nicest'.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each definition and 1 for examples.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mama, may I go to the shop?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for capitals and comma, 1 for the question mark.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Story books, poems, magazines, comics, newspapers (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: I was tired, but I finished sweeping.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a suitable conjunction (but or yet) and 1 for the comma.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: A nonverbal cue is a message sent without words. Examples: a smile shows happiness; a thumbs-up shows approval.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 for each example.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: I don't have any seeds (or: I have no seeds). English uses only one negative word here.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a correct sentence, 2 marks for the explanation.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: She is kind and patient. When Cherop pulled up a maize plant by mistake she did not scold but gently explained how to tell weeds from maize.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a trait, 2 marks for the reason.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Go out of the classroom, walk along the corridor and go past the office to the gate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct preposition.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: It cannot spread by playing, shaking hands, sharing a plate or hugging.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct fact.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: gently, angrily, quickly
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: The children put loaves and tomatoes in the boxes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for children, loaves and tomatoes and boxes (award 3 for all correct).

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: My comes before a noun (This is my bag). Mine stands alone (The bag is mine).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sentence and 1 mark for the difference.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Today we swept the compound and planted a tree.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for swept and 1 for planted.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read the whole form and its instructions, get the facts ready, write neatly in the spaces using block letters if asked, fill every space, check the spelling and sign if needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: making, running, playing, lying
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct spelling.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Put your fingers on your throat and say the sounds. You feel a buzz with /d/ because it is voiced, but no buzz with /t/, which is whispered.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the buzz with /d/, 1 mark for no buzz with /t/.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look at the speaker and keep quiet until the speaker has finished a whole idea. Nodding to show you follow is also correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct habit.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hi Kamau. Please come to my birthday party on Saturday at 3 o'clock at my home. Thank you. Ann.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for greeting, 1 for day, time and place, 1 for politeness and name.

60. (4 marks)
   Answer: With a noun, enough comes before it: enough food. With an adjective, enough comes after it: tall enough.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each position and 1 mark for each example.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: The bus had left before I arrived. (Or: When I arrived, the bus had left.)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 'had left' and 1 for the linking word.

62. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two: photographs, cartoons, maps, charts, advertisements.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
